newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bond prices closed lower on Thursday, but above the day's minimums after prices succumbed to the negative tone and generalised profit-taking on other major bourses, dealers said.
Fewer-than-expected U.S. weekly jobless claims amplified the market's downard trajectory, although the Bundesbank's expected decision to leave its rates steady had little impact.
The market is expecting consumer prices, due Friday, to have moderated to 3.6 percent in September from 3.7 percent in August - a number which would be considered neutral for the market.
Despite the decline for the day, analysts said bonds continued on firm footing although short-term evolution would depend on Friday's data.
"The short-term outlook for bonds will depend largely on tomorrow's CPI," an analyst said.
